Week 2 Assignment — Working with Data in Python

Assignment Information

Item Details
Week Week 2
Topic Working with Data in Python using a Labour Force Survey Dataset
Marks 5 Marks
Duration 1 Hour
Submission Format Google Colab notebook link
Attempts One Attempt Only
Access Lecturer Passcode Required

Assignment Purpose

This assignment tests whether students can use the Week 2 materials to begin working with real data in Python.

Students should demonstrate that they can:

  • open and save a Google Colab notebook
  • import the pandas library
  • load an Excel dataset into Python
  • understand the difference between data and a variable dictionary
  • inspect rows, columns, data types, and missing values
  • generate descriptive statistics
  • produce frequency tables
  • write short economic interpretations from output

The purpose is not memorizing code.

The purpose is learning how to move from:

raw dataset -> Python output -> economic interpretation

Required Materials

Material Link
Labour Force Survey Dataset Download LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx

Before You Begin

  1. Go to Google Colab
  2. Go to:
File -> Save a copy in Drive
  1. Rename your notebook using:
Week02_IndexNumber_Name.ipynb

Example:

Week02_2024BA12345_Perera.ipynb
  1. Download the Labour Force Survey dataset.
  2. Complete all tasks in your saved Google Colab notebook.

Dataset

This assignment uses:

LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx

The Excel workbook contains two sheets:

Sheet Purpose
LFS_Data Main dataset with individual-level labour force information
Variable Dictionary Explanation of variable names, labels, types, and coding

The dataset contains:

1000 observations
20 variables

Each row represents one individual.

Each column represents one characteristic of that individual.

Task 1 — Start the Notebook

Instructions

Run:

print("Week 2 assignment started successfully")

Then write your name and index number in a Markdown cell.

Question

In 2-3 sentences, explain why Google Colab is useful for beginners learning data analytics.

Task 2 — Import pandas

Instructions

Run:

import pandas as pd

Question

Why do economists and data analysts use libraries such as pandas instead of writing every command from scratch?

Task 3 — Load the Dataset

Instructions

Use the direct website method:

dataset_url = "https://kanishkawerawella.github.io/ECN4199_Website/data/LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx"

data = pd.read_excel(dataset_url, sheet_name="LFS_Data")
dictionary = pd.read_excel(dataset_url, sheet_name="Variable Dictionary")

If the direct website method does not work, upload the downloaded Excel file into Colab and use:

data = pd.read_excel("LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx", sheet_name="LFS_Data")
dictionary = pd.read_excel("LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx", sheet_name="Variable Dictionary")

Questions

  1. What does the LFS_Data sheet contain?
  2. What does the Variable Dictionary sheet explain?
  3. Why should analysts read the variable dictionary before interpreting a dataset?

Task 4 — Inspect the Dataset

Instructions

Run the following commands:

data.head()
data.tail()
data.shape
data.columns
data.info()

Questions

  1. How many observations are in the dataset?
  2. How many variables are in the dataset?
  3. Name five variables that are useful for labour market analysis.
  4. Are all variables numerical? Explain using examples.

Task 5 — Use the Variable Dictionary

Instructions

Display the variable dictionary:

dictionary

Then identify the meaning of these variables:

  • Employment_Status
  • Monthly_Wage_LKR
  • Education_Level
  • Internet_Access
  • Unpaid_Care_Hours_Weekly

Question

Choose any three variables from the list above and explain why each variable may be useful for economic or labour market analysis.

Task 6 — Summary Statistics

Instructions

Run:

data.describe()

Questions

  1. What is the average age of individuals in the dataset?
  2. What is the average household size?
  3. What is the average monthly wage?
  4. What is the maximum monthly wage?
  5. What is the average number of unpaid care hours per week?

For each answer, write one short interpretation.

Task 7 — Frequency Tables

Instructions

Run:

data["Sex"].value_counts()
data["Sector"].value_counts()
data["Education_Level"].value_counts()
data["Employment_Status"].value_counts()
data["Internet_Access"].value_counts()

Questions

  1. How many males and females are included in the dataset?
  2. Is the sample more urban or more rural?
  3. Which education category appears most frequently?
  4. How many individuals are employed, unemployed, and inactive?
  5. How many individuals have internet access?

Task 8 — Simple Labour Market Interpretation

Using your outputs from Tasks 6 and 7, write a short interpretation of the dataset.

Your answer should include:

  • at least three numerical findings
  • at least two categorical findings
  • one possible economic question that could be studied using this dataset

Recommended length:

150-200 words

Task 9 — Reflection

Write a short paragraph answering:

Why is Python useful for analysing Labour Force Survey data?

Your answer should refer to:

  • automation
  • reproducibility
  • large datasets
  • variable dictionaries
  • interpretation

Mark Allocation

Component Marks
Correct notebook setup, naming, and pandas import 0.5
Correct loading of LFS_Data and Variable Dictionary 0.75
Dataset inspection using head(), tail(), shape, columns, and info() 0.75
Correct summary statistics and frequency tables 1.25
Economic interpretation of outputs 1.25
Submission formatting and sharing access 0.5
Total 5.0

Before submitting:

  3. Rename the notebook correctly.
  4. Set sharing access to:
Anyone with the link -> Viewer

  2. Submit the link through the Week 2 submission form.

Common Errors

Problem 1 — File Not Found

Possible causes:

  • dataset not uploaded
  • incorrect filename
  • file uploaded to the wrong Colab session

Problem 2 — Forgetting Quotes

Wrong:

pd.read_excel(LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx)

Correct:

pd.read_excel("LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx", sheet_name="LFS_Data")

Problem 3 — Wrong Sheet Name

Wrong:

pd.read_excel("LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx", sheet_name="Data")

Correct:

pd.read_excel("LFS_Hypothetical_Dataset.xlsx", sheet_name="LFS_Data")

Academic Integrity

Students may use lecture materials and course notes.

However:

  • copied notebooks are not allowed
  • copied interpretations are not allowed
  • AI-generated answers without understanding are unacceptable
  • all interpretations must be written in the student’s own words

Students are responsible for all submitted work.
